prior_exposure: Public journal synopsis and task brief already described lost light and two moths; no fully blind audience claim.
description: A pale, round-eyed moth follows a swinging amber lantern across a teal room toward an arched doorway. The door closes between them; the moth drops to the sill, small and drooping. The closer view reveals another moth inside the doorway with the lantern above its shoulder. Its wing curves around the light. As the two turn toward one another, their wings and thin hands reach under the lantern. The last image balances both faces around one warm glow.
judgment: Keep. The switch from a large empty room and shut door to two faces and joined hands makes a small story of exclusion becoming welcome legible in the drawings. Cream wings with eye spots, antenna gestures, changing wing silhouettes and lantern framing make this a crafted encounter, beyond moving markers. The literal motion and six-second pacing are not established by viewing stills.
notes_comparison: Maker notes describe a window and shutter, which I read visually as an arched doorway and door. The sheltering of the lantern and the final offer agree with the visible sequence. That setting ambiguity does not obscure the encounter; I cannot claim an unprompted audience interpretation because I had read the public synopsis.
verdict: The crafted visual sequence earns a second look. This is an independent non-author art judgment, not source acceptance or a project milestone decision.
